lines.text: OpenAI just released a new AI model that's built to use a computer, like you do.
It's called GPT-6.1 Terra. It's made for computer use, visual reasoning, coding and everyday work.
The big deal is price. In the API, it costs half as much as the older GPT-5.6 Terra: one dollar per million input tokens.
And OpenAI says it's better. On a test of professional computer tasks, it scored 15 points higher than the old Terra, at about a third of the cost.
On the Terminal-Bench coding test, it solved about half the tasks. The old Terra managed about one in five.
It's out now for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users in ChatGPT and Codex, and for developers in the API.
Why it matters: AI that works your apps for you just got a lot cheaper. But for the hardest coding jobs, OpenAI still points to its bigger models.
